context: The Active Prompt page needs a quick way to trigger the execute command. This questionnaire clarifies the exact button placement, appearance, and behavior for copying the execute command text to the clipboard.

questions.question-text: Where should the execute command clipboard button be placed in the Active Prompt page?

options.label: In the sticky control panel (the top banner with execution mode buttons)
options.pros: Always visible when scrolling, grouped with other action buttons, quick access from any part of the page
options.cons: Makes the banner more crowded, less space for existing buttons

options.label: As a standalone button above the sticky control panel
options.pros: Clearly separated from other controls, highly visible, doesn't interfere with existing layout
options.cons: Not sticky - will scroll out of view, requires scrolling to top to use

options.label: As a button within the Prompt tab content area
options.pros: Contextually placed near the prompt text, doesn't clutter the control panel
options.cons: Only visible when Prompt tab is active, requires tab switching if user is in another tab

options.label: As a floating action button (FAB) in the bottom-right corner
options.pros: Always visible and accessible, modern UI pattern, doesn't interfere with existing layout
options.cons: May cover content on smaller screens, less discoverable for new users

questions.recommendation-rationale: The sticky control panel is the logical location since it contains other action buttons (Create Modification, Complete) and execution mode controls. Adding it there provides quick access from anywhere on the page and keeps all actions centralized.

questions.question-text: What should be the button label and icon for the execute command clipboard button?

options.label: Icon only: clipboard icon (bi-clipboard)
options.pros: Minimal space usage, clean appearance, standard icon meaning
options.cons: May not be immediately clear what text will be copied, relies on tooltip for clarity

options.label: Text and icon: 'Execute' with play icon (bi-play-fill)
options.pros: Clear action indication, familiar terminology from the execute command concept
options.cons: Slightly misleading - button copies text rather than executing directly

options.label: Text and icon: 'Copy Execute Cmd' with clipboard icon (bi-clipboard)
options.pros: Explicitly states what will be copied, clear purpose, no ambiguity
options.cons: Longer text takes more space, may wrap on smaller screens

options.label: Text and icon: 'Execute ⎘' with clipboard-check icon (bi-clipboard-check)
options.pros: Concise, combines execute concept with clipboard action, modern appearance
options.cons: May still be slightly unclear without tooltip explanation

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option C provides the clearest user experience by explicitly stating the action. While it uses more space, clarity is more important than brevity for this feature. Users will immediately understand what happens when clicking the button.

questions.question-text: Should the button provide visual feedback when the text is copied to the clipboard?

options.label: Show a success alert at the top of the page
options.pros: Consistent with existing alert patterns in the UI, clear confirmation message
options.cons: Requires manual dismissal or auto-hide timing, adds clutter to the page

options.label: Temporarily change the button text/icon to 'Copied!' with checkmark
options.pros: Immediate visual feedback at the interaction point, no additional UI elements needed, auto-reverts after a few seconds
options.cons: May not be noticed if user looks away quickly

options.label: Show a small toast notification near the button
options.pros: Non-intrusive, modern UX pattern, appears at interaction point
options.cons: Requires additional CSS/JS for toast implementation, may interfere with other elements

options.label: No visual feedback - rely on system clipboard confirmation
options.pros: Minimal implementation, users can verify by pasting
options.cons: No confirmation that action succeeded, poor user experience, users may click multiple times

questions.recommendation-rationale: Changing the button text to 'Copied!' with a checkmark provides immediate, clear feedback right where the user clicked. This is a widely-used pattern in modern web applications and requires minimal implementation - just a temporary text/icon change that reverts after 2-3 seconds.

questions.question-text: What exact text should be copied to the clipboard?

options.label: Exact text as specified: 'Follow the instructions in file `.rdd/prompt-snippets/execution.md`'
options.pros: Matches the exact format specified in the prompt, uses backticks for file path
options.cons: Backticks may not render properly if pasted in plain text contexts

options.label: Plain text version: 'Follow the instructions in file .rdd/prompt-snippets/execution.md'
options.pros: Works in all contexts, no special characters that might cause formatting issues
options.cons: Slightly different from the specified format

options.label: GitHub Copilot chat link format: 'Follow instructions in [rdd.execute.prompt.md](file:///full/path/.github/prompts/rdd.execute.prompt.md)'
options.pros: Uses the actual prompt file that redirects to execution.md, provides clickable link in Copilot chat
options.cons: Requires determining the full absolute path dynamically, more complex implementation

options.label: Markdown link format: 'Follow the instructions in [execution.md](.rdd/prompt-snippets/execution.md)'
options.pros: Creates a clickable link in markdown-aware contexts, still readable as plain text
options.cons: May not work as expected in all Copilot chat contexts

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A follows the exact format specified in the prompt requirements. The backticks are intentional for code formatting and should work correctly when pasted into GitHub Copilot chat. This provides the most predictable behavior.

questions.question-text: Should the button be always enabled or have conditional enabling logic?

options.label: Always enabled - copying execute command text should always be available
options.pros: Users can always prepare the execute command, simple implementation, no confusion about when it's available
options.cons: Button is enabled even when there might not be an active prompt (though this should not happen)

options.label: Disabled when no active prompt exists
options.pros: Provides visual feedback about system state, prevents confusion
options.cons: More complex logic, adds another state to manage, execute command can still technically be run without active prompt

options.label: Disabled when execution mode is 'no-action'
options.pros: Aligns button state with execution readiness, guides users to set appropriate mode
options.cons: May prevent users from copying the command to prepare for later execution, overly restrictive

options.label: Always enabled but show a warning if execution mode is 'no-action'
options.pros: Allows copying at any time while providing helpful guidance
options.cons: Additional complexity with warning logic, may interrupt workflow

questions.recommendation-rationale: The button should always be enabled because copying text to clipboard is a harmless operation. Users may want to copy the execute command text before setting the execution mode, or prepare it for use. The framework's validation will handle inappropriate execution attempts.
